content.text: {"answer":"Use variable (any-precision) mixture-of-experts by quantizing experts at different bit-widths and selecting the precision at runtime based on router signals or token/expert sensitivity. DyMoE targets edge/mobile constraints by dynamically quantizing experts at runtime using expert importance skewness and depth-adaptive scheduling, and it overlaps I/O via look-ahead prefetching to reduce TTFT and improve TPOT on commercial edge hardware [2]. GEMQ and AlphaQ tackle the expert-wise bit-allocation needed for mixed precision, either via global optimization plus router fine-tuning to handle router shifts after quantization [5] or via calibration-free bit allocation using expert-wise heavy-tailed spectral structure under a global bit-budget [3].\n\nTo directly support “variable precision” at inference, DPA-MoE encodes expert feed-forward weights into prefix-decodable chunks so the routed experts can be any-precision using live router gate scores, letting one checkpoint operate under multiple effective weight budgets without retraining/re-encoding (with modest throughput overhead) [7]. On mobile NPUs, Quant.npu further shows the practicality of fully static integer quantization plus a sensitivity-guided adaptive mixed-precision scheme for lower latency [4]. MoBiQuant complements this by addressing precision-dependent outlier migration with a token-aware router that selects optimal inference precision per token [1].","grounded":true}
